shared_capability: A single reusable dataset freshness monitor that compares each dataset's last-update time against policy-configured thresholds and reports each dataset as fresh, stale, or unknown (never measured), grouped by owner team.

distinct_needs.need: Know when the engine_test_runs dataset is stale using a 60-minute threshold, checked before every hotfire review, so that the dashboard does not silently show old test data.
A weekly SLA report on the freshness of NCR tables, grouped by owner team, in which any dataset never measured is reported as unknown rather than fresh.
One shared, reusable freshness-check capability to replace three hand-rolled per-engineer checks, where thresholds are policy configuration rather than code.

symptoms.symptom: A review dashboard silently displayed three-day-old engine test data.
No freshness SLA report for NCR tables exists that is grouped by owner team (inferred from the request asking for one); the request also states that unmeasured datasets must not appear fresh.
Three forward deployed engineers each built their own freshness checks with different thresholds.

underlying_problem: Dataset freshness is not measured by any shared, policy-driven mechanism, so stale data goes unnoticed and datasets that have never been measured can look the same as fresh ones. (Inference from the three requests.)
observed_facts: syn-req-001: the hotfire review dashboard silently showed three-day-old engine test data last week.
syn-req-001: the stakeholder wants to know when the engine_test_runs dataset is stale, with a 60-minute threshold, before every review.
syn-req-002: the BOM cost dashboard broke when an upstream column was renamed, and nobody noticed for days.
syn-req-002: the stakeholder wants a check that compares each table schema against its declared contract and reports drift by field.
syn-req-003: the stakeholder needs an SLA report on the freshness of NCR tables for the weekly ops review, grouped by owner team.
syn-req-003: a dataset that has never been measured must be reported as unknown, not fresh.
syn-req-004: three forward deployed engineers each hand-rolled their own dataset freshness checks with different thresholds.
syn-req-004: the team wants one shared, reusable capability where thresholds are policy configuration, not code.
interpretations: Inference: syn-req-001, syn-req-003 and syn-req-004 all ask for dataset freshness measurement against a threshold, so they share one capability. Each has a different consumer: a review gate, a weekly SLA report, and a platform reuse need.

Inference: syn-req-002 asks about schema drift against a contract, not time-based freshness. It shares a monitoring pattern (declared expectation versus observed state) but not the same check, so it is not consolidated. It could later be a sibling capability built on the same policy and reporting layer.
Inference: the 'unknown, not fresh' rule from syn-req-003 is a design requirement that the shared capability should carry for all consumers.
Inference: syn-req-004's policy-configured thresholds are what would let the 60-minute value from syn-req-001 and the NCR thresholds from syn-req-003 live in one place.

Inference: the three hand-rolled checks in syn-req-004 are probably the same kind of logic as the checks behind syn-req-001 and syn-req-003, which suggests they could be migrated onto the shared capability. This is not stated in any request.
unknowns: Whether syn-req-002 (schema contract drift) should be built into the same capability or kept as a separate capability. No request decides this.
Where each dataset's last-update timestamp comes from, and whether every dataset in scope has one. No request says.
The list of NCR tables and the source of truth for owner-team mapping. Not stated in syn-req-003.
The freshness threshold for NCR tables. Only syn-req-001 states a value (60 minutes, for engine_test_runs).
Who owns and approves threshold policy values.
Whether the 'before every review' check in syn-req-001 is a hard gate that blocks the dashboard or only a warning or display flag.
How reports and alerts should be delivered (dashboard, scheduled report, or notification).
Which thresholds the three forward deployed engineers currently use, and whether their existing checks should be migrated.
Whether a dataset with no timestamp and a dataset that has never been checked should both be reported as unknown.
